stories.headline: 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, tsunami threat issued for nine countries in Central and South America
stories.title: 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, tsunami threat issued for nine countries in Central and South America
stories.summary: Panama, Oct 10 : An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 struck off Panama on Friday night. The US Embassy in Panama warned of possible aftershocks and potential tsunami threats across nine countries in Central and South America. In a post shared on X, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said the earthquake occurred at 11:26 pm IST on October 9 at a depth of 10 kilometres. According to the details shared, the epicentre was located 206 kilometres southwest of Panama City, Panama. Meanwhile, the US Embassy in Panama said a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck in La Pitaloza, Panama, at 12:56 local time on October 9, with the location approximately 14 kilometres southwest of Pitaloza Arriba. The embassy warned that aftershocks capable of causing damage may occur. It also said the US Tsunami Warning System had issued potential tsunami threats for Costa Rica, El Salvador, Peru, Mexico, Guatemala, Panama, Nicaragua, Colombia and Ecuador. “Strong and unusual currents and unpredictable surges may occur along the shore,” the embassy said, advising US citizens in the affected areas to stay away from damaged structures and monitor local emergency broadcasts and official guidance for updates. The embassy urged people to avoid damaged areas and refrain from entering damaged buildings. It also advised those near the coast to move to higher ground and follow instructions issued by local authorities. It further warned people to be prepared for possible power and communication outages.

stories.headline: Assam: Flood-Hit Jerenga Pathar Sees Economic Revival Through Thriving Fish Trade
stories.title: Assam: Flood-Hit Jerenga Pathar Sees Economic Revival Through Thriving Fish Trade
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Daily fish harvests of 15-25 quintals boost local trade at flood-hit Jerenga Pathar, with loads of dried indigenous fish transported to Jagiroad.

NAZIRA: Historic Jerenga Pathar, associated with Assam's rich history and the venue of the centenary biennial session of the Axam Xahitya Xabha in 2017, is witnessing a revival of economic activity following the devastating floods of July 19.
The floods left thousands of families in Jerenga Pathar and adjoining areas struggling to rebuild their lives.
For nearly two months, floodwater remained trapped across vast agricultural fields, causing extensive damage to crops and disrupting the livelihoods of farmers.
However, as the water receded, numerous water bodies and pond-like depressions formed across the fields, creating favourable conditions for fish to thrive.
With agricultural activities still affected by the damaged fields, the abundance of fish has opened up an alternative source of income for hundreds of flood-hit families.
According to local sources, around 15 to 20 quintals of fish are being harvested daily from the water bodies.
The growing trade has benefited more than 100 families and provided fresh business opportunities for local traders.

A variety of indigenous and other fish species, including moua, puti, singora, singi, magur, pabho, kawoi, goroi, tura, rohu, borali, mrigal, grass carp and silver carp, are available in the local market.
Fish harvested from Jerenga Pathar is being transported to markets across Sivasagar and Jorhat districts.
Meanwhile, traders are drying indigenous fish on bamboo racks under the sun to cater to the growing market for dried fish.
Large quantities of dried fish are reportedly being transported daily to Jagiroad, known for its major dried-fish market.

stories.headline: Woman Moves Karnataka High Court Seeking LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case
stories.title: Woman Moves Karnataka High Court Seeking LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A woman has approached the Karnataka High Court seeking a direction to the police to initiate the process for issuance of a Look Out Circular (LOC) against her husband, a France-based working professional accused of cruelty and dowry harassment.
The wife contends that her husband remains in India only pending reissuance of his allegedly lost passport and that his departure would prejudice the ongoing investigation.
Advocate Angad Kamath mentioned the matter yesterday before Justice Anant Ramananth Hegde.
The matter is likely to be taken up next week.

The plea challenges an October 8 order of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court rejecting her application under Section 175(3) read with Section 94 BNSS, seeking a direction to the Investigating Officer to request issuance of an LOC and intimate the Regional Passport Officer about the pending criminal case.
"A Look Out Circular opened on the direction sought can be deleted the day this Petition fails; the departure of Accused No. 1 cannot be undone by any order thereafter," the plea states.
The couple married in November 2022.
On September 30, the wife lodged a complaint alleging physical, mental and economic cruelty, unlawful demands for money and retention of her wedding gold.
An FIR was registered under Sections 85, 352 and 351(2) BNS and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
According to the plea, the husband ordinarily resides in France, where he has a valid residence permit, an indefinite-term employment contract and an apartment.
He arrived in India on August 23 and had a confirmed return flight for October 1, but did not board it.
He subsequently reported his passport lost.

stories.headline: When Can ECI Choose Not To Hold Bye-Election? Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Interpretation Of S.151A RP Act
stories.title: When Can ECI Choose Not To Hold Bye-Election? Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Interpretation Of S.151A RP Act
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently reserved judgment on the interpretation of Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which prescribes a six-month period for holding bye-elections to fill casual vacancies in Parliament and State Legislatures, subject to certain exceptions.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Augustine George Masih and Justice Sandeep Mehta reserved the judgment in the Election Commission of India's plea challenging a December 2023 Bombay High Court judgment directing it to hold a bye-election for the Pune Lok Sabha constituency.

Section 151A provides that a bye-election to fill a casual vacancy "shall be held within a period of six months from the date of the occurrence of the vacancy." However, the proviso states that the provision will not apply if "the remainder of the term of a member in relation to a vacancy is less than one year." A further exception applies where the Election Commission, in consultation with the Central Government, certifies that it is difficult to hold the bye-election within the six-month period.
The question is from what point the one-year period under the first exception is to be calculated.
The Bombay High Court held that the relevant date is the date on which the vacancy occurs.
The Pune Lok Sabha seat fell vacant on March 29, 2023 while the term of the 17th Lok Sabha was due to expire over 14 months later on June 16, 2024.
The High Court held that the one-year exception in Section 151A did not apply a bye-election had to be conducted.
The ECI has contended that the six-month period available to the ECI for conducting the bye-election has to be accounted for while determining whether the one-year exception applies.
The issue arose from the vacancy in the Pune Lok Sabha constituency following the death of sitting MP Girish Bapat on March 29, 2023.
The term of the 17th Lok Sabha was due to end on June 16, 2024.
The ECI declined to hold a bye-election, issuing a certificate under Section 151A stating that it was difficult to conduct the election.

It cited, among other reasons, its engagement with elections and preparations for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and the fact that the candidate elected in a bye-election would have only a limited period in office.

stories.headline: GenZ deserves better than undeclared Emer-GenZ: Tharoor slams govt
stories.title: GenZ deserves better than undeclared Emer-GenZ: Tharoor slams govt
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 10: Hitting out at the Modi government, Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Saturday claimed that Delhi is witnessing a "war-like deployment", and said "our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ". He said the government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression. Tharoor, who was in Berlin this week, said he returned to the national capital after 2 am and has rarely seen anything like what Delhi is witnessing now. "Checkpoints every few hundred metres, concrete barriers and spike strips laid across our roads, a "war-like" deployment of 22,000 police and paramilitary across the city, 250 trains cancelled and 45 metro stations closed, and reports of young people being detained from their own homes and the streets in and around Delhi -- all to prevent citizens from peacefully raising questions about the integrity of our elections," he said on X. "Most regressive (as well as repressive) is the suspension of the internet in the heart of the national capital," the former Union minister said. Freedom of movement stands completely shackled, he said. Jantar Mantar was designated precisely so that citizens could voice dissent in the centre of Delhi, and today even the roads leading to it have been declared out of bounds, the MP from Thiruvananthapuram said. "One is entitled to ask where this extraordinary manpower and urgency disappear when women in our capital need protection," Tharoor said. Noting that those detained will have to be released, Tharoor asked if the protesters simply return on Monday, will the authorities lock down the national capital all over again. "Our GenZ deserves better than an undeclared Emer-GenZ," he said. A government confident in the fairness of its elections would welcome questions about them, whereas one that turns its capital into a fortress to avoid them only deepens the very suspicions it seeks to suppress, he said. "The government should provide answers, not lathis; expression, not repression," Tharoor asserted. Barricades will do nothing to restore faith in the Election Commission, and the sooner it answers the public's questions, the sooner calm will be restored, he said. "The strength of a democracy is measured by how it treats those who question its working, and by that measure, what we have seen today is utterly shameful and unconscionable," Tharoor said. Delhi Police on Saturday detained over 500 protesters, who were trying to reach Jantar Mantar for the proposed CJP stir against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, police sources said over 600 people with criminal records were also detained across all 15 districts of the national capital as part of preventive measures. Police personnel have been deployed at strategic locations across the city, particularly in areas leading to Jantar Mantar and other sensitive locations, to prevent any untoward incident. The security arrangements include heightened surveillance and monitoring of the movement of people suspected of attempting to disrupt law and order. Police are also keeping a close watch on possible mobilisation efforts ahead of the proposed demonstration. The proposed protest has prompted heightened security measures in the national capital, with police maintaining a strict vigil to prevent any breach of peace. Delhi Police has denied permission to the CJP to hold its proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar, citing security considerations and procedural requirements. Police have said that prohibitory orders are in force in the New Delhi area and appealed to people to abide by the restrictions. The CJP has called the proposed demonstration against the CEC over allegations of voter-list manipulation during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and changes relating to Form 6, used for voter registration.

stories.headline: "I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes": Trump slams Nobel Committee for awarding Navi Pillay
stories.title: "I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes": Trump slams Nobel Committee for awarding Navi Pillay
stories.summary: Washington, October 10 : US President Donald Trump on Saturday criticised the Norwegian Nobel Committee for awarding the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay, claiming that he deserved the honour for his role in resolving conflicts across the world. In a lengthy post on Truth Social on Friday (local time), Trump questioned Pillay's credentials and accused her of being opposed to Israel, while reiterating his claim that he had settled eight wars and deserved multiple Nobel Peace Prizes. “This is the woman who received the Nobel Peace Prize over the Great United States of America, whose Representative, ME, settled eight Wars, and many other things. I know nothing about this woman, and neither does anyone else!” Trump said. He added, “In fact, to the best of my knowledge, no one ever heard of her other than the fact that she, very obviously, hates Israel.” Trump listed eight conflicts that he claimed to have settled, including Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, Israel and Iran, Egypt and Ethiopia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Israel and Hamas. “I settled 8 Wars, with letters being sent from every President and Prime Minister from the countries that I helped to the Norwegian Nobel Committee, and I’m about to settle, or win, two more, Iran and, Russia/Ukraine,” he said. “Based on my record of PEACE, a record like no one else has ever achieved, I agree! I got back all of the hostages in Israel, including the final 28, both living and dead, and worked with Hamas to do it -- Nobody believed this was possible!” Trump added, while citing his other claimed achievements in international diplomacy and security. He further asserted that he had prevented Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and claimed to have helped avert conflicts in other regions, including tensions involving North Korea, South Korea, Japan, China and Taiwan. “In actuality, I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes, not just 1,” Trump said, referring to the conflicts he claimed to have resolved. The US President also criticised the United Nations, saying it had not helped in resolving the conflicts he cited. “In all of the Wars that I have settled, I never spoke to the United Nations--they were of no help,” he said. “The United States of America, represented by me, as your President, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t. This is an indelible stain on Norway, one that will never be forgotten,” Trump added. He further declared that the Nobel Peace Prize had been “forever discredited by a handful of Radical Ideologues who are Anti-Democracy, and Enemies of Civilization!” Trump's remarks came after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated his support for the US President's Nobel Peace Prize bid. “In recognition of his outstanding contribution, Pakistan had nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize,” Sharif said, adding that he hoped Trump's efforts to promote peace would receive recognition. Meanwhile, the United States announced additional sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday (local time), citing concerns over American sovereignty and the threat posed by the international judicial body. The announcement came on the same day the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Pillay. In a statement, the Norwegian Nobel Committee said Pillay had demonstrated exceptional courage and integrity in advancing a more comprehensive global legal order and had played a significant role in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide were prosecuted. Pillay, a former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, has served as a judge on South Africa's High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory until recently and is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide. In response to the India-Pakistan ceasefire, New Delhi has consistently disputed Trump's claims while remaining steadfast in rejecting any external mediation. India has reiterated that the ceasefire understanding during Operation Sindoor was reached only after Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) reached out to his Indian counterpart to request a halt in military action. India had launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 last year as a decisive, targeted response to destroy terror infrastructure across Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The anti-terror operation was carried out to dismantle terror bases that were utilised to plan the horrific April 22 terrorist attack in Pahalgam. Following effective Indian strikes that dismantled key terror launchpads, the operation was paused on May 10 after a formal request from the Pakistani side. (ANI)

stories.headline: Supreme Court forms panel for judicial well-being on World Mental Health Day
stories.title: Supreme Court forms panel for judicial well-being on World Mental Health Day
stories.summary: Supreme Court forms panel for judicial well-being on World Mental Health Day
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set up a standing committee on judicial well-being for officers across the country.
The move seeks a lasting system to address stress and strengthen justice delivery.

The Supreme Court on Saturday constituted a standing committee on judicial well-being to create a structured institutional mechanism for identifying and addressing issues affecting the professional and personal well-being of judicial officers.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant constituted the committee, which will be chaired by sitting Supreme Court judge Justice K V Viswanathan.
In a statement, the top court said the move was made under the aegis of the Supreme Court of India and coincided with World Mental Health Day.

"In a significant initiative aimed at promoting the mental and physical well-being of judicial officers across the country, Justice Surya Kant, Chief Justice of India, has constituted a standing committee on judicial well-being under the aegis of the Supreme Court of India, coinciding with World Mental Health Day," the statement said.

Besides Justice Viswanathan, the committee will include Dr Savita Malhotra, former dean, PGIMER Chandigarh, and Professor and Head, Department of Psychiatry, Rajat Mitra, psychologist, Director and Co-founder, Swanchetan Society for Mental Health, Mrinal Kanwar, advocate-on-record in the apex court, and Aarti Singh, Registrar (J), Centre for Research and Planning of the top court.
The court said the initiative marked an important step towards recognising judicial well-being as an essential part of an effective, independent and sustainable justice delivery system.

It said judicial officers work under demanding conditions, often dealing with heavy caseloads, long working hours, complex decision-making, administrative pressures, and emotionally challenging and sensitive cases.

"Recognising these occupational demands, the Supreme Court has established the committee to provide a structured institutional mechanism for identifying and addressing issues affecting the professional and personal well-being of judicial officers," it said.
The statement said judges' well-being was not merely a matter of individual welfare, but was closely linked to the efficiency, quality and sustainability of the administration of justice.
It said the committee would function as a continuing institutional platform to review existing and emerging challenges related to judicial well-being.

opening: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday said it will conduct an open market operation (OMO) sale auction of government securities worth Rs 25,000 crore on October 13.
The central bank has offered six government securities for the auction, with maturities ranging from March 2030 to April 2034.
body: These include 7.88 per cent government security (GS) 2030, 6.10 per cent GS 2031, 7.95 per cent GS 2032, 7.26 per cent GS 2033, 7.18 per cent GS 2033, and 7.10 per cent GS 2034, according to a notification.
The RBI has not specified individual sale amounts for the six securities and retains the discretion to decide the quantum of each security to be sold.
It may also accept bids for less than the notified aggregate amount and adjust the total sale marginally to account for rounding-off.
The central bank reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids, either wholly or partially, without assigning any reason.
OMO sales involve the sale of government securities by the central bank, which withdraws liquidity from the banking system in exchange for the securities.
Currently, liquidity in the banking system is estimated to be in surplus of around Rs 3.88 lakh crore as of October 8.
Since two months, the RBI has been doing various VRRR auctions to absorb excess surplus liquidity from the banking system and align the overnight money market rates to the repo rate.

The banking system was flushed with liquidity due to heavy mobilisation of FCNR (B) deposits by banks, as the mobilisation brought foreign currency into the system, while subsequent swaps with the RBI provided rupee liquidity to banks.
Besides FCNR(B) inflows, month-end government expenditure, including payments toward salaries and pensions, also added to liquidity in the banking system.

On October 6, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, during the post-monetary policy press conference, said the huge banking system liquidity is to be absorbed within the current financial year through various means such as currency leakage, the Reserve Bank's liquidity operations, and banks' reserve requirements.

stories.summary: Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi said the shutdown was in clear violation of the October 9 order of the Supreme Court, which had emphasised that the authorities must not cause any hardship or suffering to ordinary commuters through a blanket ban

article_sentences: A Supreme Court advocate on Saturday (October 9, 2026) filed a contempt petition in the apex court on the continued “blanket shutdown across transit corridors” to and within the national capital.
Follow the updates of the Anti-CEC protests in Delhi on October 10, 2026.

Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi said the shutdown was in clear violation of the October 9 order of the Supreme Court, which had emphasised that the authorities must not cause any hardship or suffering to ordinary commuters through a blanket ban and impose restrictions in a suitable and regulated manner only ahead of and during the October 10 protests for the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Mr. Tripathi is the lead petitioner who moved the Supreme Court on the police action against youth protestors on July 20 during the NEET-UG paper leak protests.
He has sought a judicial order to initiate contempt proceedings against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, IAS; Delhi.
Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, IPS and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) Chairperson D. Thara, IAS, for alleged willful non-compliance with the court’s directions.

“Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the Bench of the Chief Justice of India, the contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicise transparent traffic and transit advisories,” the petition said.

It said the “deliberate recalcitrance” has severely crippled public life across the National Capital Territory, stranding essential travelers, and amounts to an intentional attempt to bypass and undermine the authority and majesty of the court.

“The Supreme Court had recorded the commitment of the Solicitor General of India and categorically held that there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains or essential railway transit; Transport authorities were mandated to switch from blanket ‘prohibition’ to proportionate ‘regulation’ so as to avoid any harassment or inconvenience to the citizens; Any such regulatory framework and traffic advisory was required to be widely published across print and digital media immediately,” the petition said.
In its October 9 order, the apex court had sought compliance reports from the authorities within four days.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks High Court To Re-Hear Plea Against Goa Female Weightlifter's Selection As Coach
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks High Court To Re-Hear Plea Against Goa Female Weightlifter's Selection As Coach
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently set aside the Bombay High Court's order, which disallowed Goa weightlifter Vaishnavi S. Ugadekar from selection to the post of Coach (Grade-IV) in Weightlifting.

A bench comprising Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar observed that the High Court decision dismissed the plea without impleading or hearing her, despite her being one of only two candidates competing for the post.
This arose during the selection process where Ugadekar had raised a complaint regarding the fairness of the selection, following which the State Government directed that the tests be re-conducted.
The other candidate filed a writ petition challenging the decision before the High Court, which passed the impugned order without making Ugadekar a party.
The Court has now set aside this order and restored the writ petition for fresh consideration on merits, directing that Ugadekar be impleaded and both candidates be heard.
The Court also directed that its interim order shall continue during the pendency of the writ petition and requested the High Court to decide the matter at the earliest.

It noted: "Considering that the appellant and respondent No. 4 are the only two candidates competing for the post, we deem it appropriate to direct the High Court to decide the matter afresh after affording an opportunity of hearing to both parties.

Consequently, the impugned order is set aside, and the Writ Petition preferred by respondent No. 4 is restored to its original number for a decision afresh on merits upon hearing all parties to the Writ Petition, including the present appellant who shall be impleaded as a party before the High Court."
Further, it has directed that the High Court should decide the matter at the earliest.
The bench has however, clarified that the High Court shall decide the matter afresh on its own merits, uninfluenced by either its earlier order or the Supreme Court's order.
Appearances: For Petitioner(s) Mr. Salvador Santosh Rebello, AOR Ms. Sneha Bhargava, Adv.
Mr. Ankit Rana, Adv.

stories.headline: Ranji Trophy 2026-27: Defending champion J&K begins title defence against Madhya Pradesh
stories.title: Ranji Trophy 2026-27: Defending champion J&K begins title defence against Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir’s strengths and vulnerabilities were on display in its Irani Cup 2026 defeat, but it will be bolstered by the return of Auqib Nabi fresh off his debut for the national team.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A week after the Irani Cup defeat exposed the cracks in its armour, Jammu and Kashmir gets a chance to reset on familiar turf.
The defending champion begins its Ranji Trophy campaign against Madhya Pradesh at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium on Sunday, hoping to leave that disappointment behind and find its feet again.
India pacer Auqib Nabi’s availability offers a timely boost, although J&K has rested Umar Nazir, who claimed six wickets in the Irani Cup.
Nasir Lone and Sunil Kumar provide further pace options, while Umran Malik, despite being with the squad, has not been considered.
The bigger concern, however, is the batting.
J&K squandered a first-innings lead against Rest of India before collapsing in the second innings.
Shubham Khajuria, Qamran Iqbal, Abdul Samad and captain Paras Dogra will need to shoulder the responsibility if the host is to make its home advantage count.
Building partnerships and avoiding another collapse will be central to its plans.
Madhya Pradesh, meanwhile, has spent the past week in Srinagar acclimatising to the conditions and arrives without any injury concerns.
Led by Shubham Sharma, it will miss Rajat Patidar and Venkatesh Iyer but retains considerable batting depth through Yash Dubey, Harsh Gawli and Himanshu Mantri.
The bowling attack, spearheaded by the experienced Avesh Khan and featuring Kuldeep Sen, has the pace to trouble the hosts.
Saransh Jain and Kumar Kartikeya add experience to the spin department, giving MP a balanced attack.
